title: Nail products, acrylics and dip powders: hazards and safety data sheets
audience: Mobile nail technicians who store, carry and use nail products at client locations
learningOutcomes: Name the nail product types that WorkSafe Victoria identifies as a hazard in the beauty industry
Find and read the safety data sheet for a product and state the controls it requires
Explain why each product in the kit must be on a register and have a current safety data sheet held at the visit
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson are listed in officialReferences: WorkSafe Victoria (hazardous substances in the hairdressing and beauty industry; safety data sheets; safety basics).

instruction.heading: The product types that carry a named hazard
instruction.body: WorkSafe Victoria's guidance for the hairdressing and beauty industry names nail acrylics and dip powders as products that can give off mists and dust during use. Those airborne particles and vapours are the reason the product's safety data sheet and the workplace controls matter at every visit, not only at the start of a job. The guidance also names eyelash extension glue and chemical peels, which are outside this course, and those are covered in the mobile beauty course. The guidance does not list every chemical in a nail product, and this lesson does not state the contents of any product. The technician must read the safety data sheet for each product in use, because the contents differ between brands and between formulas of the same brand.

instruction.heading: Reading a safety data sheet
instruction.body: A safety data sheet describes a product's hazards, the first aid steps, the handling and storage requirements, and the personal protective equipment the product needs. The business must hold a current safety data sheet for every product it uses, and it must be accessible at the place where the product is used. WorkSafe Victoria's guidance on safety data sheets (reviewed 30 July 2022) requires an up-to-date sheet for every product. When a technician takes a product to a client's home, the sheet for that product must travel with the kit, either as a paper copy or in a form that can be opened without a network connection. The technician reads the handling section before the first use of a new product and follows the controls it lists. A product whose sheet cannot be found is not used until the sheet is obtained from the supplier.

instruction.heading: Keeping a register and applying controls
instruction.body: WorkSafe's safety basics guidance (reviewed 30 July 2022) states that the employer needs a register listing every hazardous substance on site. For a mobile business, the register is the list of products in each kit or vehicle, with the safety data sheet location for each. Controls are chosen from the safety data sheet and the risk assessment for the visit, and they may include ventilation, the use of the product in the amount the service needs, and the personal protective equipment the sheet names. Mists and dust from acrylics and dip powders are a reason to keep the product containers closed when not in use, to avoid pouring or filing over the client's skin or the floor where dust can be breathed, and to check the room's ventilation before the work starts. The specific controls for each product are set by its sheet and by the business's approved procedure, held in {{business:procedures.approved_sop}}.

procedure: Check the product against the approved product list before it goes into the kit
Confirm that a current safety data sheet for the product is held, and that it is accessible at the visit
Record the product on the register of hazardous substances for the business
Read the handling and personal protective equipment sections of the sheet before the first use
Set up the room for the work, including ventilation, and keep containers closed when not in use
Use the product in the amount the service needs, and do not decant unused product back into the stock container
Dispose of waste product and used materials as the sheet and the business procedure direct

workedExamples.situation: A technician adds a new dip powder to the kit, and the supplier's sheet is not yet on file. The client's appointment is in two days.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the product be used at the appointment, and what must happen first?
workedExamples.reasoning: The product cannot be used until its current safety data sheet is held and has been read. The technician asks the supplier for the sheet and records the request. If the sheet cannot be obtained before the appointment, the service that uses this product is not offered at that visit. The technician may offer a service that uses only products with sheets on file, and records the change to the booking.

workedExamples.situation: At a home visit, the technician notices that the dust from a dip powder is settling on the client's furniture while the nails are being filed.
workedExamples.reasoning: The dust is a sign that the controls for the work may not be enough. The technician stops filing, checks the safety data sheet's controls for the product, and adjusts the set-up, for example by keeping the product container closed, improving ventilation where the room allows, or using a method the sheet and the procedure allow. The technician records the event, and reviews the risk assessment for that location before the next visit.

equipmentAndPpe: Safety data sheet for each product in the kit, held on paper or offline
Register of hazardous substances for the business, with sheet locations
Gloves that the product's safety data sheet specifies
Eye protection where the sheet or the approved procedure requires it
Sealable containers for products and for waste

commonErrors.error: Using a product without a current safety data sheet on file.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not use a product until its current sheet is held and has been read. Keep the sheet with the kit.

commonErrors.error: Assuming two products from the same brand have the same hazards.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the sheet for each product and each formula. Contents differ between products.

commonErrors.error: Returning unused product to the main container.
commonErrors.prevention: Decant only the amount needed for the visit, and discard or clean the dish after use, as the approved procedure directs.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WorkSafe Victoria names nail acrylics and dip powders as products that can give off mists and dust in the beauty industry. This is a confirmed hazard for Victorian businesses.
WorkSafe Victoria requires an up-to-date safety data sheet for every product (safety data sheet guidance, reviewed 30 July 2022). This applies to the mobile business as to any other.
WorkSafe Victoria states that employers need a register listing every hazardous substance on site (safety basics guidance, reviewed 30 July 2022).

The contents of specific nail products, including monomers and solvents, are not stated in this lesson. Their hazards and controls come only from each product's safety data sheet. Exposure limits for individual substances are UNCONFIRMED for this course.

qualityStandard: Every product in the kit has a current safety data sheet held and readable at the visit
The register lists every product, with the location of its sheet
Controls used at each visit match the sheet and the approved procedure
No product is used without a sheet on file
documentationEvidence: Register of hazardous substances, with sheet locations and review date
Safety data sheet held for each product, with the supplier and date received
Record of any incident involving product mists, dust or spills, and the review that followed
summary: Acrylics and dip powders are named by WorkSafe Victoria as hazards in the beauty industry
Each product's safety data sheet sets its hazards and controls
A product without a current sheet on file is not used
The register and the sheets must be kept with the kit for every visit

knowledgeChecks.question: A technician wants to use a new nail product that has no safety data sheet on file. What should happen?
options: Use it once for a small test, then file the sheet later
Do not use it until the current sheet is held and read
Use it if the supplier's website describes it as safe

knowledgeChecks.question: Which product types does WorkSafe Victoria name as a hazard in the beauty industry?
options: Nail acrylics and dip powders, which can give off mists and dust
Only hand sanitiser, because it contains alcohol
No nail product, because they are sold for salon use
